officialTitle: Twice-daily compared with once-daily thoracic radiotherapy in limited small-cell lung cancer treated concurrently with cisplatin and etoposide

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: We studied 417 patients with limited small-cell lung cancer.
design.notes: Intergroup trial; all patients received cisplatin plus etoposide with thoracic radiotherapy beginning with the first chemotherapy cycle. Same total dose in both arms; the comparison is fractionation/overall treatment time.

clinicalQuestion: In limited-stage SCLC treated with concurrent cisplatin-etoposide, does accelerated twice-daily thoracic radiotherapy improve survival over once-daily radiotherapy to the same total dose?

pico.intervention: Cisplatin-etoposide with concurrent twice-daily accelerated thoracic radiotherapy starting with cycle 1
pico.comparator: Cisplatin-etoposide with concurrent once-daily thoracic radiotherapy to the same total dose
pico.outcomes: Overall survival; oesophagitis and other toxicity

arms.label: Twice-daily thoracic RT
arms.regimen: Cisplatin + etoposide with concurrent twice-daily thoracic radiotherapy
arms.dosing: 45 Gy given twice daily over three weeks; four 21-day cycles of cisplatin plus etoposide
arms.doseSourceQuote: All the patients received four 21-day cycles of cisplatin plus etoposide. We randomly assigned these patients to receive a total of 45 Gy of concurrent thoracic radiotherapy, given either twice daily over a three-week period or once daily over a period of five weeks.

arms.label: Once-daily thoracic RT
arms.regimen: Cisplatin + etoposide with concurrent once-daily thoracic radiotherapy
arms.dosing: 45 Gy given once daily over five weeks; four 21-day cycles of cisplatin plus etoposide
arms.doseSourceQuote: All the patients received four 21-day cycles of cisplatin plus etoposide. We randomly assigned these patients to receive a total of 45 Gy of concurrent thoracic radiotherapy, given either twice daily over a three-week period or once daily over a period of five weeks.

publications.title: Twice-daily compared with once-daily thoracic radiotherapy in limited small-cell lung cancer treated concurrently with cisplatin and etoposide.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Twice-daily treatment beginning with the first cycle of chemotherapy significantly improved survival as compared with concurrent once-daily radiotherapy (P=0.04 by the log-rank test). After a median follow-up of almost 8 years, the median survival was 19 months for the once-daily group and 23 months for the twice-daily group.

The survival rates for patients receiving once-daily radiotherapy were 41 percent at two years and 16 percent at five years. For patients receiving twice-daily radiotherapy, the survival rates were 47 percent at two years and 26 percent at five years.

safety.sourceQuote: Grade 3 esophagitis was significantly more frequent with twice-daily thoracic radiotherapy, occurring in 27 percent of patients, as compared with 11 percent in the once-daily group (P<0.001).

strengths: Randomised phase III intergroup trial with long follow-up
Isolates the effect of fractionation by keeping total dose identical between arms
limitations: The once-daily comparator used a total dose that is lower than many contemporary once-daily schedules, limiting comparison with modern high-dose once-daily regimens
Older staging and radiotherapy techniques (pre-PET, pre-conformal planning)
Higher rate of severe oesophagitis with twice-daily treatment

clinicalImplications.text: Established early concurrent twice-daily accelerated thoracic radiotherapy with cisplatin-etoposide as a reference standard for limited-stage SCLC, at the cost of more severe oesophagitis.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Start thoracic radiotherapy early with chemotherapy; the twice-daily schedule is the comparator against which later once-daily trials (CONVERT and the CALGB/RTOG trial) were measured.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 9920950. No hazard ratio is reported in the abstract. Registry number not printed in the abstract.
